newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up on NY jump, futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up on NY jump, futures expiry.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday after staging a strong rally prompted by the upturn in U.S. markets overnight and the expiry of October Hang Seng index futures, brokers said.
"The rise is a combination of demand stimulated by U.S. market gains and futures expiration, said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas."
The Hang Seng Index closed 213.30 points higher at 12,405.47, off an afternoon peak of 12,428.16. Turnover soared to HK$7.48 billion, considerably higher than Tuesday's HK$5.53 billion.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average put on 34 points to 6,007 on Tuesday and the U.S. long bond rallied 2-4/32 to yield 6.68 percent following positive economic reports suggesting that U.S. inflationary forces were relatively quiescent.

October futures, which expired on Wednesday, rose 144 points to close at 12,374, still at a discount to the index at its close, but just at a par with the Hang Seng's average for the day. The November contract rose 210 points to 12,448 on healthy volume.
While trading in the market's blue chip counters was heavy, brokers said the volume was across the board, covering mid-cap issues included in the Morgan Stanley Capital Index for Hong Kong.
The focus on index components and the day's heavy volume indicate active programme trading, one broker said.

Technically, the market's recent correction bottomed out at the 12,200 level and the index is back on its bull run course, said John Schofield, regional technical analyst at NAVA SC Securities in his Asia Chartline.
Schofield said investors should stick to the market leaders, in particular Cheung Kong which still had considerable upside.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market followed closely by the property sector. China-incorporated H shares tended lower.
Conglomerate CITIC Pacific jumped HK$0.90 to HK$37.50.
Sun Hung Kai Properties led the market with a gain of HK$2.50 to HK$87.50. The share goes ex-dividend on November 15. Wharf Holdings added HK$1.30 to HK$31.60 on turnover of HK$112.17 million.
HSBC, the day's most active issue, gained HK$2.00 to HK$156.50 on heavy trade of HK$699.79 million. Hang Seng Bank also regained HK$2.00 to HK$91.75.
